linkedin:
> It means access is being denied as a consequence of a legal demand, per RFC 7725.

Two things surprise people. First, the blocker is often not the website: the spec explicitly says the responding server might not be the origin, and names ISPs and search engines as most affected. Second, a correct 451 should tell you who blocked it, in a `Link` header with `rel="blocked-by"`, and should explain the demand in the response body.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/http-error-451-unavailable-for-legal-reasons/
